title: Pkarr / Mainline DHT
body:
**Provider or primitive; confirmed upstream source**

Signed small DNS records, native DHT and HTTP relays: [Pkarr](https://github.com/pubky/pkarr)

**Signer / authentication**

Ed25519 records plus Ghostly participation/content authentication

**Runtime/platform route**

Native UDP; browser/extension HTTP relay

**Ghostly status and next gate**

**Current, scoped**: rendezvous and bounded short text. Validate UDP separately from relay tests, packet budget, stale records and retry limits. No general file/history store.

title: WebRTC
body:
**Provider or primitive; confirmed upstream source**

Data channels and media APIs: [W3C](https://www.w3.org/TR/webrtc/)

**Signer / authentication**

DTLS/session binding plus Ghostly peer authentication

**Runtime/platform route**

Browser/extension; native WebView features vary

**Ghostly status and next gate**

**Current, scoped**. Test ICE/STUN/TURN paths, WebKit permissions, suspend/resume and media capability separately. A TURN relay is infrastructure.

title: Iroh
body:
**Provider or primitive; confirmed upstream source**

Endpoint connectivity: [official docs](https://docs.iroh.computer/)

**Signer / authentication**

Iroh endpoint identity bound to Ghostly participation/transcript

**Runtime/platform route**

Current Ghostly native Rust adapter; other targets need independent validation

**Ghostly status and next gate**

**Current native**, Draft 102. Keep **Iroh** as the name. Generic QUIC peers do not automatically speak Iroh. Measure relay use and runtime availability.

title: HyperDHT / Hyperswarm
body:
**Provider or primitive; confirmed upstream source**

Hole punching and encrypted Noise streams: [HyperDHT](https://github.com/holepunchto/hyperdht)

**Signer / authentication**

Transport key plus Ghostly transcript binding

**Runtime/platform route**

Current native bundled runtime; browser UDP is not assumed

**Ghostly status and next gate**

**Current native**, Draft 103. Validate bootstrap, platform packaging, network changes and endpoint-key mismatch.

title: Tor
body:
**Provider or primitive; confirmed upstream source**

Onion/SOCKS integration based on [Tor specifications](https://spec.torproject.org/)

**Signer / authentication**

Onion/service authentication plus Ghostly identity; not the same key

**Runtime/platform route**

Proposed native daemon/embedded route; browser requires an explicitly supported path

**Ghostly status and next gate**

**Research**. Specify leak policy, DNS/discovery path, latency, dependency distribution and fail-closed behavior. Do not send UDP or silently fall back to direct IP under a Tor-only policy.

title: Local discovery / broadcast
body:
**Provider or primitive; confirmed upstream source**

Opt-in LAN discovery; mDNS candidate: [RFC6762](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6762.html)

**Signer / authentication**

Advertisements are hints; authenticate before joining

**Runtime/platform route**

Proposed native networking; browser needs supported bridge/API

**Ghostly status and next gate**

**Candidate**. Multicast vs custom broadcast must be chosen; scope to interface/LAN, expire advertisements, never broadcast secrets or social identity by default. QR discovery is a separate route.

title: QR / explicit invitation
body:
**Provider or primitive; confirmed upstream source**

Current invite parser and [admission draft 800](800-invite-join.md)

**Signer / authentication**

Bearer bootstrap vs authenticated admission are distinct

**Runtime/platform route**

Current camera/image/paste where permissions allow

**Ghostly status and next gate**

**Current scoped UX**, future admission semantics proposed. QR carries a bounded invitation; it is neither a live transport nor proof of the person who displayed it.

title: GossipSub
body:
**Provider or primitive; confirmed upstream source**

[libp2p GossipSub 1.1 specification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/libp2p/specs/master/pubsub/gossipsub/gossipsub-v1.1.md)

**Signer / authentication**

Group-authenticated envelope above mesh; topic is not authorization

**Runtime/platform route**

JS/Rust/Go libp2p profiles require a selected common stack

**Ghostly status and next gate**

**Planned 9xx**, number to be defined. Needs 900 membership/epochs, limits, scoring, abuse resistance, churn tests. No automatic durable history or total ordering.

title: Pear / Holepunch components
body:
**Provider or primitive; confirmed upstream source**

[Pear runtime](https://docs.pears.com/), [Hypercore](https://github.com/holepunchto/hypercore), [Autobase](https://github.com/holepunchto/autobase)

**Signer / authentication**

Append-only data signatures, writer authority and group keys require composition

**Runtime/platform route**

Pear/Bare/Node or native bindings; each module differs

**Ghostly status and next gate**

**Research** for distribution, storage and multiwriter state. Keet is a product; these libraries do not establish a supported Keet app API or redistribution right for its private internals.

title: Generic QUIC profile
body:
**Provider or primitive; confirmed upstream source**

[RFC9000](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9000.html)

**Signer / authentication**

TLS identity and Ghostly binding must be specified

**Runtime/platform route**

Proposed native QUIC library; browser WebTransport is a different API/profile

**Ghostly status and next gate**

**Candidate**, conditional value beyond Iroh. Define ALPN, framing, endpoint discovery, certificates, flow control and NAT behavior before assigning a profile. No Iroh rename.

title: libp2p connectivity profile
body:
**Provider or primitive; confirmed upstream source**

[official stack](https://docs.libp2p.io/) and selected transport specifications

**Signer / authentication**

libp2p peer identity plus explicit Ghostly binding

**Runtime/platform route**

Candidate JS/native implementation; per-transport availability

**Ghostly status and next gate**

**New suggestion / research**. Could reuse relay/muxing infrastructure; choose an exact profile and avoid duplicating discovery blindly. Do not claim all implementations support all transports.

title: WebSocket relay profile
body:
**Provider or primitive; confirmed upstream source**

[RFC6455](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6455.html)

**Signer / authentication**

E2E Ghostly envelope above authenticated service connection

**Runtime/platform route**

Browser, extension, native, server

**Ghostly status and next gate**

**New suggestion / candidate** for constrained networks. Server sees metadata; quota, retention, offline receipts and operator policy need explicit contracts.

title: Cashu
body:
**Provider / signer route**

Cashu SDK + chosen mint; wallet controls bearer proofs, mint backs redemption

**Runtime and platform route**

Current app integration; upstream TS/Rust/Python options

**Confirmed evidence, Ghostly status, restriction / next decision**

**Current, scoped**, [Draft 201](201-cashu.md), [NUTs](https://github.com/cashubtc/nuts), [libraries](https://docs.cashu.space/). Mint trust/custody must be visible. Verify mint/unit allowlist, quote states, duplicate redemption, keysets and recovery; NUT07/09 availability is not universal seed recovery.

title: Lightning BOLT11
body:
**Provider / signer route**

One active `LightningProvider` source per profile and mode; the Cashu mints are the default and only shipped source; external node/wallet providers below plug into the same contract

**Runtime and platform route**

Current app subset; provider/runtime determines expansion

**Confirmed evidence, Ghostly status, restriction / next decision**

**Current subset**, [Draft 203](203-lightning.md), [provider guide](../../packages/browser/src/engine/paymentAdapters/PROVIDERS.md). Sources declare create/pay/lookup capabilities; payments are journaled before spending and an unknown outcome is only reconciled. Validate invoice signature/network/amount/expiry in executing wallet. A displayed invoice or peer receipt is not settlement evidence.

title: Ark via Arkade
body:
**Provider / signer route**

Arkade TypeScript SDK, operator and wallet signer

**Runtime and platform route**

TypeScript SDK 0.4.74 selected for the in-development browser adapter; native parity unverified

**Confirmed evidence, Ghostly status, restriction / next decision**

**In development**: [wallet docs](https://docs.arkadeos.com/wallets/getting-started/introduction), [security model](https://docs.arkadeos.com/learn/core-concepts/security-and-trust-model). Preserve exit transaction data, measure operator/chain dependencies and exit costs. Selected second implementation; local regtest send/receive, HD return spend and receipt reconciliation verified. Shared Cashu/Ark review flow is implemented; encrypted local backup restore verified; exits and broader platform/UI coverage remain incomplete. Not release-ready. See [Draft 202](202-arkade.md).

title: Ark via Bark
body:
**Provider / signer route**

Second's Bark SDK (WebAssembly build `@secondts/bark` 0.24.0, bark 0.7.1) and Second's server; wallet signer in the SDK

**Runtime and platform route**

Web/WASM selected for the in-development browser adapter (one path for web, extension offscreen page and Desktop WebView); Rust crate, Barkd REST daemon and UniFFI bindings upstream

**Confirmed evidence, Ghostly status, restriction / next decision**

**In development, Testnet only**: [Web SDK](https://second.tech/docs/bark-sdk/wasm), [connection details](https://second.tech/docs/connection-details), [backups](https://second.tech/docs/backups). Checked 2026-09-23: **not wire compatible with Arkade** (Bark refuses Arkade addresses; out-of-round payments only reach the same server), so it is its own method `bark` / `payments-bark/1`. Signet server `ark.signet.2nd.dev` (faucet needs a GitHub login); local regtest send/receive, on-chain board, chat Send/Request and payee-side receipt verification verified; Mainnet not enabled although Second runs one. Seed-only recovery is server-dependent; exits, Lightning via Bark and funded signet remain open. See [Draft 204](204-bark.md).

title: Bitcoin on-chain
body:
**Provider / signer route**

`bitcoin` payment method through one active `OnchainProvider` source per profile and mode (none by default); BDK/Core/other wallet as provider modules

**Runtime and platform route**

Native library/node first; explicit external wallet/PSBT route for browser

**Confirmed evidence, Ghostly status, restriction / next decision**

**Contract in place, no provider shipped**: [draft section](200-payments.md#on-chain-bitcoin-draft), [provider guide](../../packages/browser/src/engine/paymentAdapters/PROVIDERS.md), [BDK](https://bitcoindevkit.org/), [Core RPC](https://bitcoincore.org/en/doc/), [PSBT](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0174.mediawiki). Address validation per network, sign-at-review/broadcast-at-approval and same-transaction reconciliation implemented; coin selection, fee policy, change, RBF/reorg and chat requests remain to be specified.

title: Fedimint
body:
**Provider / signer route**

Fedimint web SDK (`@fedimint/core` canary, pinned; WebAssembly client in Ghostly's own worker, one OPFS database per federation), v1 mint/ln modules, the federation's gateway

**Runtime and platform route**

Web/WASM selected for the in-development browser adapter (one path for web, extension offscreen page and Desktop WebView); upstream Rust client for native

**Confirmed evidence, Ghostly status, restriction / next decision**

**In development, Testnet only**: [technical reference](https://docs.fedimint.org/), [web SDK](https://github.com/fedimint/fedimint-sdk). Its own method `fedimint` (`fedimint-ecash/1`, paired-payments list only); notes are never Cashu tokens. Checked 2026-09-24/25 on a regtest federation (fedimintd/gatewayd 0.12.1, LND gateway) in e2e/infra: join by invite after a preview, ecash in over the gateway, notes out/redeemed/taken back, a chat Send in ecash reviewed and redeemed, a request paid over the gateway's Lightning, Lightning out to another node; the `fedimint` Lightning source. Journal before spend, operation-log reconciliation, federation identity (id, network) and recovery-based restore are implemented; Mainnet, iroh federations, gateway refunds and multi-guardian failures remain open. See [Draft 2xx](2xx-fedimint.md).

title: Spark
body:
**Provider / signer route**

Breez SDK Spark (WebAssembly `@breeztech/breez-sdk-spark` 0.26.0, nodeless), the same SDK and seed as the Breez Lightning source; Spark's operators and Lightspark's SSP

**Runtime and platform route**

One WebAssembly path for web, extension offscreen page and Desktop WebView

**Confirmed evidence, Ghostly status, restriction / next decision**

**In development**: its own method `spark` (announced in the session's payment list only), [Draft 2xx](2xx-spark.md). Spark to Spark with Spark addresses (static: the wallet's identity) and Spark invoices (per request: amount, expiry, id), no Lightning hop. Testnet on Breez and Lightspark's hosted regtest (no API key, proven); Mainnet behind a Breez API key, labelled real bitcoin. "Use for Lightning too" makes the same wallet the Breez source. Unilateral exit, Spark tokens and the faucet (reCAPTCHA) remain open.

title: Liquid
body:
**Provider / signer route**

Elements/Liquid wallet integration, chosen signer and network service

**Runtime and platform route**

Native wallet/node candidate; browser through an explicitly supported wallet API

**Confirmed evidence, Ghostly status, restriction / next decision**

**Candidate**: [Liquid developer docs](https://docs.liquid.net/docs/welcome-to-liquid-developer-documentation-portal). Separate L-BTC and issued assets; validate asset IDs, confidential-transaction/blinding support, fees and federation/peg assumptions. Not equivalent to Bitcoin L1.

title: USDT through Tether WDK
body:
**Provider / signer route**

`@tetherto/wdk-wallet-evm` 1.0.0-beta.19; separate encrypted seed, configured EVM RPC, ETH for gas

**Runtime and platform route**

Shared browser/Tauri adapter; local Anvil transaction tests; native financial runtime not verified

**Confirmed evidence, Ghostly status, restriction / next decision**

**Experimental implementation**: Ethereum chain 1 canonical USDT, six decimals; send/receive/review/reconcile implemented. Signed TEST-USDT transactions on Anvil chain 31337 validate recovery but are not Tether-issued USDT. No mainnet funds were used. Issuer controls, gas costs, RPC trust, two-block confirmation and operational limitations remain explicit. See [implementation scope](../USDT-INTEGRATION.md).

title: Manual external wallet
body:
**Provider / signer route**

Every request and every receive shown as QR, text and a `lightning:` / BIP 21 URI (`lightning=`, `ark=`); the payee's own source settles

**Runtime and platform route**

Copy/QR everywhere; the link opened by the system on desktop (`open_payment_link`) and by the extension's background page

**Confirmed evidence, Ghostly status, restriction / next decision**

**Current subset**, [200](200-payments.md#paid-from-another-wallet), [203](203-lightning.md#paid-from-another-wallet). “Opened wallet” and “I paid” are never settlement: the payee's wallet sees the invoice, transaction or virtual output, marks the request paid and tells the payer; “I paid” only makes it look now. No wallet callback is relied on.

title: Lightning address / LNURL-pay
body:
**Provider / signer route**

LUD-16/06/01/17/12/09 paying through the active Lightning source; parsing and checks in core, fetching in the engine

**Runtime and platform route**

Same on web, extension and desktop (the service must allow CORS); a local LNURL server in e2e

**Confirmed evidence, Ghostly status, restriction / next decision**

**Current subset**, [Draft 205](205-lnurl.md). Domain named before any fetch, bounded fetches, invoice amount and metadata commitment checked. Receiving on an address needs a server the person runs and is out of scope; LUD-18/21 and BOLT 12 open.

title: LND
section: Providers, chain data and signer boundaries
body:
**Capability / provider contract**

Invoice creation, payment execution/status through node API

**Signer and runtime restrictions**

Node controls keys; scoped credentials/macaroons, authenticated connection; native/server adapter or constrained bridge, never expose admin credential to apps

**Gate and official source**

**Candidate**. Test timeout/TrackPayment recovery and node availability. [LND docs](https://docs.lightning.engineering/lightning-network-tools/lnd).

title: Core Lightning
section: Providers, chain data and signer boundaries
body:
**Capability / provider contract**

Node RPC/payment/invoice integration

**Signer and runtime restrictions**

Node signer; local RPC or explicitly configured authenticated service; provider permission model must be pinned

**Gate and official source**

**Candidate**. Separate node implementation from rail; failure/status and least-privilege tests. [Official API](https://docs.corelightning.org/reference).

title: NWC
section: Providers, chain data and signer boundaries
body:
**Capability / provider contract**

Delegated remote-wallet request/response via Nostr relays

**Signer and runtime restrictions**

Per-connection wallet authorization, **not** a social identity proof; wallet may be custodial or self-hosted

**Gate and official source**

**Candidate**. Negotiate supported commands, budgets and revocation; do not require Nostr identity feature to use NWC. [NIP47](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nostr-protocol/nips/master/47.md).

title: WebLN
section: Providers, chain data and signer boundaries
body:
**Capability / provider contract**

Browser/provider integration for Lightning requests

**Signer and runtime restrictions**

Injected/approved wallet provider; capabilities differ and native support needs bridge

**Gate and official source**

**Candidate**, not a separately numbered WISP. [WebLN guide](https://www.webln.guide/). Test provider missing, approval canceled and ambiguous execution.

title: Bitcoin Core RPC
section: Providers, chain data and signer boundaries
body:
**Capability / provider contract**

Wallet operations, chain observation and broadcast, separately permissioned

**Signer and runtime restrictions**

Personal node/server; RPC credentials stay in privileged backend; wallet may be watch-only/external-signer

**Gate and official source**

**Candidate**. Never proxy arbitrary node RPC through a public shared app. [RPC reference](https://bitcoincore.org/en/doc/).

title: Electrum protocol
section: Providers, chain data and signer boundaries
body:
**Capability / provider contract**

History/UTXO/status/broadcast service

**Signer and runtime restrictions**

Server observes wallet queries; protocol endpoint is not a wallet signer

**Gate and official source**

**Candidate**. Verify headers/proofs as applicable, server/network identity and privacy policy. [Protocol](https://electrum-protocol.readthedocs.io/en/latest/).

title: Esplora
section: Providers, chain data and signer boundaries
body:
**Capability / provider contract**

HTTP chain query, fee and transaction broadcast API

**Signer and runtime restrictions**

Indexer observes queried addresses; no signer

**Gate and official source**

**Candidate**. Bound responses and distinguish accepted broadcast from confirmation. [API](https://github.com/Blockstream/esplora/blob/master/API.md).

title: BDK
section: Providers, chain data and signer boundaries
body:
**Capability / provider contract**

Wallet construction/synchronization primitives with selected backends

**Signer and runtime restrictions**

Rust/library integration; descriptors and signing strategy selected separately

**Gate and official source**

**Candidate**. Bind a wallet instance/network to its observer and signer; not a hosted payment rail. [BDK](https://bitcoindevkit.org/).

title: PSBT exchange
section: Providers, chain data and signer boundaries
body:
**Capability / provider contract**

Standard unsigned/partially signed transaction handoff

**Signer and runtime restrictions**

Hardware/software signers, files or QR; format/version/script support varies

**Gate and official source**

**Candidate**. Validate every returned input/output/change/fee against authorized intent. [BIP174](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0174.mediawiki).

title: Personal wallet / Umbrel
section: Providers, chain data and signer boundaries
body:
**Capability / provider contract**

User-selected LND/CLN/Bitcoin/Bark or another installed provider

**Signer and runtime restrictions**

Self-hosted service with explicit pairing; remote connectivity, uptime, credential isolation

**Gate and official source**

**Candidate deployment composition**, not a new rail. [Umbrel app packaging](https://github.com/getumbrel/umbrel-apps), [Bark Wallet installation](https://second.tech/docs/bark-wallet/install.md). No personal service connected in this research.

title: Proof
body:
**Data / action**

Context-bound evidence of a key or qualified account authorization

**Trust and permission boundary**

Nonce, audience/domain, participation binding, lifetime and independent verification; no automatic login/publication permission. **Nostr: current** ([301](301-nostr.md)).

title: Profile
body:
**Data / action**

Name, avatar, bio and source metadata

**Trust and permission boundary**

Self-described content; local cache, provenance and manual nickname precedence; fetching is not proof. **Nostr: experimental** ([3xx](3xx-nostr-social.md)): kind 0 on request or by an explicit setting, from the person's relays, cached with source/time/stale.

title: Social graph
body:
**Data / action**

Follows/followers, memberships, links between identities

**Trust and permission boundary**

Direction, source, visibility and freshness; no inference that every edge is reciprocal or trusted. **Nostr: experimental**: kind 3 on request; "follows you" / "you follow" / "you both follow" hints, each with its direction and time, computed locally.

title: Content read/search
body:
**Data / action**

Posts, replies/comments, reactions, feeds and query results

**Trust and permission boundary**

Pagination, content limits, moderation, ranking source and cache policy; index results may disagree. **Nostr: experimental**: a key's kind-1 notes, newest first, paginated, hidden by the person's own kind-10000 mute list; no feed, no ranking, no search.

title: Publication
body:
**Data / action**

Create/edit/delete content, follow/unfollow, react

**Trust and permission boundary**

Separate explicit authorization/scope; network propagation and deletion limits. **Nostr: experimental**: a capability off by default; note, follow/unfollow, profile update through NIP-07/NIP-46 only, each drafted by the app, confirmed and shown as public; no deletion, no reactions.

title: Nostr
body:
**Confirmed upstream primitive / source**

Signed events; [NIP07](https://github.com/nostr-protocol/nips/blob/master/07.md), [NIP46](https://github.com/nostr-protocol/nips/blob/master/46.md)

**Signer, runtime and trust distinction**

Browser external signer or remote bunker; event signature verification separate from relay delivery

**Ghostly status / next gate**

**Current** proof provider (2026-09-23): NIP-07 and NIP-46 sign one kind-30078 event carrying the [identity statement](300-peer-proofs.md#implementation-2026-09-23-identity-proofs), never published to a relay; verified by each contact (event id recomputed, BIP-340). Profile (kind 0), follows (kind 3), notes (kind 1) and publication (kinds 1/3/0 through the person's signer) are the **experimental** [Nostr social layer](3xx-nostr-social.md), each a separate capability: on request or an explicit setting, from the person's own relays, bounded and self-described, publication off by default.

title: NsecBunker
body:
**Confirmed upstream primitive / source**

Remote signer implementation: [upstream repository](https://github.com/kind-0/nsecbunkerd)

**Signer, runtime and trust distinction**

NIP46 provider; user key can differ from remote signer key; hosting and approval policies matter

**Ghostly status / next gate**

**Candidate signer**, not a new identity rail. Check maintenance, current NIP compatibility, refusal/timeouts/revocation; no deployment assumed.

title: Pubky / Ring
body:
**Confirmed upstream primitive / source**

[AuthToken protocol](https://github.com/pubky/pubky-homeserver/blob/main/docs/AUTH.md), [Ring routes](https://github.com/pubky/pubky-ring)

**Signer, runtime and trust distinction**

Ring documents scoped homeserver authorization, not a general Ghostly arbitrary-message signing API

**Ghostly status / next gate**

**Experimental/deferred; standard storage proof unfinished**. A temporary homeserver commitment is a research path, with server trust, independent fetch, freshness and cleanup to validate. Do not modify Ring or expose auth tokens as peer proofs.

title: Pubky profiles / graph / content
body:
**Confirmed upstream primitive / source**

Existing local [profile experiment](PUBLIC-PROFILES.md), upstream homeserver/indexer separation

**Signer, runtime and trust distinction**

Cached indexed metadata must identify source; an indexer response is not automatically a user-signed payload

**Ghostly status / next gate**

**Deferred**, broader social adapters **research**. Separate source data, indexes, publication permissions and multiple-indexer disagreement.

title: Keet
body:
**Confirmed upstream primitive / source**

[keet-identity-key](https://github.com/holepunchto/keet-identity-key) supplies derivation primitives

**Signer, runtime and trust distinction**

Compatible key material does not prove control of an existing Keet account or expose a supported signer/profile API

**Ghostly status / next gate**

**Compatible-import experiment deferred; existing-app bridge blocked**. Need public supported signing/export/API and license evidence; do not ask for a seed or infer compatibility from Ed25519.

title: OpenPGP / PGP
body:
**Confirmed upstream primitive / source**

[RFC9580](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9580.html) signatures, key/subkey formats

**Signer, runtime and trust distinction**

The person's own gpg signs; OpenPGP.js 6 verifies, loaded lazily; hardware-backed OpenPGP works unchanged

**Ghostly status / next gate**

**Experimental**: [WISP 3xx](3xx-openpgp.md). Signed once (clearsigned or detached) over the contract's binding of the OpenPGP key to a Ghostly proof key, then presented per chat without re-signing; v4/v6 keys, allowlisted algorithms (Ed25519, Ed448, ECDSA NIST/brainpool, RSA ≥ 2048), signing subkeys with back-signatures, expiry and hard/soft revocation checked at signing and now, strict size limits, minimal key shared. Fingerprint and user IDs shown with the warning that key possession is not trust in a UID/name; keys.openpgp.org is contacted only on request, and its email check is labelled as its own.

title: SSH
body:
**Confirmed upstream primitive / source**

`ssh-keygen -Y sign` signatures ([PROTOCOL.sshsig](https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/blob/master/PROTOCOL.sshsig)), namespace `ghostly`: [OpenSSH manual](https://man.openbsd.org/ssh-keygen)

**Signer, runtime and trust distinction**

The person's own `ssh-keygen` (key file, `ssh-agent` or a FIDO security key); Ghostly never sees the private key, the pasted signature is verified locally

**Ghostly status / next gate**

**Experimental providers `ssh`, `ssh-github`, `ssh-gitlab`**, [SSH · 3xx planned](3xx-ssh.md). Ed25519, ECDSA P-256/384/521, RSA (`rsa-sha2-256/512`, ≥2048 bits) and `sk-ssh-ed25519`/`sk-ecdsa` security keys (touch required), checked against real `ssh-keygen` vectors. No principals/allowed-signers file: the subject is the key fingerprint, or a forge account (row below). The key is never used for SSH authentication.

title: Bitcoin address proof
body:
**Confirmed upstream primitive / source**

Legacy signmessage and [BIP322](https://bips.dev/322/) are different formats

**Signer, runtime and trust distinction**

Wallet/device-specific message signing; script/address validation, not merely same secp256k1 curve

**Ghostly status / next gate**

**Implemented, experimental** (2026-09-23): identity-proof provider `bitcoin`, BIP-322 pinned to 2.0.0 (bitcoin/bips@4061a54) with its official vectors; simple/full for P2WPKH and P2TR key path, full for P2SH-P2WPKH and P2PKH; legacy signmessage for P2PKH only; multisig/script paths inconclusive, proof of funds refused. Paste-back from the person's wallet; "sign with my Ghostly wallet" waits for an on-chain source that signs messages. No proof of current balance, historical sender or willingness to spend. [Draft](3xx-bitcoin.md).

title: DID
body:
**Confirmed upstream primitive / source**

[DID Core](https://www.w3.org/TR/did/) verification relationships

**Signer, runtime and trust distinction**

Select a concrete DID method, resolver and proof suite; rotation/resolution may be network-dependent

**Ghostly status / next gate**

**Research family**, not one adapter. Method-specific trust, service endpoints and recovery must be chosen. A resolved document alone is not a fresh proof of possession.

title: Farcaster
body:
**Confirmed upstream primitive / source**

[Auth client](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/farcasterxyz/auth-monorepo/main/packages/auth-client/README.md) requests/verifies sign-in; separate [Mini Apps](https://miniapps.farcaster.xyz/)

**Signer, runtime and trust distinction**

Wallet signature and account/FID binding with relevant chain queries; auth relay and domain/nonce handling

**Ghostly status / next gate**

**Candidate auth/proof route**, social graph/feed/publishing **research**. Sign-in does not automatically grant publication or validate all profile data.

title: AT Protocol / Bluesky
body:
**Confirmed upstream primitive / source**

[protocol overview](https://atproto.com/guides/overview), [OAuth profile](https://atproto.com/specs/oauth)

**Signer, runtime and trust distinction**

DID/account resolution and OAuth/DPoP authorization; an app's DPoP key is not the user's repository identity key

**Ghostly status / next gate**

**Candidate account integration**, portable peer proof **research**. Separate PDS/repository data from AppView/feed/search indexes, scopes and handle changes.

title: Secure Scuttlebutt
body:
**Confirmed upstream primitive / source**

[SSB protocol guide](https://ssbc.github.io/scuttlebutt-protocol-guide/) signed feeds and replication

**Signer, runtime and trust distinction**

Feed author keys; runtime and chosen feed format matter

**Ghostly status / next gate**

**Research**. Feed replication is not a generic challenge signer; establish fresh context binding, forks, migration and supported maintained implementation before adapter selection.

title: ActivityPub / Mastodon
body:
**Confirmed upstream primitive / source**

[ActivityPub](https://www.w3.org/TR/activitypub/), [Mastodon client API](https://docs.joinmastodon.org/client/intro/)

**Signer, runtime and trust distinction**

Federated actor/server relationships and client OAuth are different from user-held key signatures

**Ghostly status / next gate**

**Candidate account/profile/social integration**, key-possession proof **unproven**. Select server/client API, instance discovery and scopes; never label OAuth account access as a hardware-backed peer proof.

title: Domain
body:
**Confirmed upstream primitive / source**

DNS TXT via [DNS over HTTPS](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8484), [RFC 8615](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8615) `/.well-known/ghostly.json`, [NIP-05](https://github.com/nostr-protocol/nips/blob/master/05.md) `nostr.json`

**Signer, runtime and trust distinction**

Control of a name, shown by publishing under it once; the resolver (and, for files, the domain's web server) sees the check; DNS answers are only as honest as the resolver unless DNSSEC validated

**Ghostly status / next gate**

**Experimental provider**, [draft 3xx](3xx-domain.md). Records name the proof key and statement id, not a participation key; private addresses refused before any web fetch; re-checked daily. Not a legal-identity or registrant claim; domain transfer keeps a record alive until the proof expires.

title: GitHub
body:
**Confirmed upstream primitive / source**

[OAuth authorization](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/oauth-apps/building-oauth-apps/authorizing-oauth-apps); published SSH keys: [GitHub](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/users/keys#list-public-keys-for-a-user), [GitLab](https://docs.gitlab.com/api/user_keys/)

**Signer, runtime and trust distinction**

OAuth is provider-authenticated account access. Published keys are public data the account holder controls; both APIs allow CORS, `github.com/<login>.keys` does not

**Ghostly status / next gate**

**Account proof without OAuth, experimental** (`ssh-github`, `ssh-gitlab`): an SSH key signs the binding and the contact's app shows "GitHub: <login> (via published SSH key)" only while that account lists the signing key; re-checked after ten minutes, the lookup disclosed to the person. See [SSH · 3xx planned](3xx-ssh.md). OAuth assertions remain a **candidate** (define audience/nonce, whom peers trust). A profile fetch alone still proves nothing.

title: OpenID Connect providers: Google, Microsoft (Entra, work/school and personal), Apple, GitLab.com, Twitch
body:
**Confirmed upstream primitive / source**

[OpenID Connect Core](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html) ID tokens, each provider's discovery document and JWKS

**Signer, runtime and trust distinction**

The provider signs an ID token whose `nonce` is the statement id; the contact checks it against the provider's published keys. **Attested by the provider**, not a key the person holds. Public clients, no secret: `id_token` responses (Apple `code id_token`, fragment, no scope; GitLab code + PKCE)

**Ghostly status / next gate**

**In development**, [draft 3xx](3xx-oidc-proofs.md). Needs the maintainer's OAuth client registrations ([checklist](../OIDC-PROVIDERS.md)); until then neither offered nor accepted.

title: Facebook
body:
**Confirmed upstream primitive / source**

[Facebook Login](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/facebook-login/)

**Signer, runtime and trust distinction**

The web login returns an access token checked through Facebook's API; its OIDC ID token ("Limited Login") exists only in the iOS SDK

**Ghostly status / next gate**

**Research**: verifying it needs a Ghostly server that checks the account and signs an attestation, which moves the trust to Ghostly.

title: X / Twitter
body:
**Confirmed upstream primitive / source**

[OAuth 2.0](https://docs.x.com/resources/fundamentals/authentication/oauth-2-0/overview)

**Signer, runtime and trust distinction**

OAuth 2.0 with PKCE, but no OpenID Connect: no signed ID token, only API access

**Ghostly status / next gate**

**Research**, for the same reason: without an ID token only a server calling X's API could attest the account.

title: LinkedIn
body:
**Confirmed upstream primitive / source**

[Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/consumer/integrations/self-serve/sign-in-with-linkedin-v2)

**Signer, runtime and trust distinction**

Signs ID tokens, but only through a code exchange that needs the client secret, and its JWKS answers without CORS

**Ghostly status / next gate**

**Research**: needs a Ghostly server; revisit if LinkedIn offers public clients.

title: Trezor
body:
**Confirmed official capability/source**

Current [Bitcoin messages](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trezor/trezor-firmware/main/common/protob/messages-bitcoin.proto) include message/transaction operations; [THP transport](https://docs.trezor.io/trezor-firmware/common/thp/specification.html)

**Runtime / physical route**

Connect/device integration candidate; WebUSB or native transport depends on model/firmware/browser

**Restriction and Ghostly gate**

**Candidate**. Pin device/firmware and exact method/script; do not infer BIP322 or arbitrary Ed25519/Nostr signing. Test on-device readable intent, cancel/disconnect, derivation path and result verification.

title: YubiKey: WebAuthn/FIDO
body:
**Confirmed official capability/source**

[WebAuthn](https://www.w3.org/TR/webauthn-3/), [Yubico](https://developers.yubico.com/)

**Runtime / physical route**

Browser/OS authenticator, USB/NFC or platform mechanism as supported

**Restriction and Ghostly gate**

**Candidate authentication**, portable Ghostly root **research**. RP ID/origin/challenge and user presence/verification are essential; credentials may be device-bound or synced. Not a general raw-signature oracle or Bitcoin signer.

title: YubiKey: OpenPGP / PIV / SSH
body:
**Confirmed official capability/source**

[OpenPGP](https://developers.yubico.com/PGP/), [PIV](https://developers.yubico.com/PIV/Introduction/YubiKey_and_PIV.html), OpenSSH route above (FIDO `sk-` SSH keys verified by the `ssh` providers)

**Runtime / physical route**

Native agent/smartcard middleware; device/firmware/slot-specific algorithms

**Restriction and Ghostly gate**

**OpenPGP applet: experimental** through the [OpenPGP proof](3xx-openpgp.md). gpg drives the card (PIN, touch policy) and Ghostly only verifies; the usual card layout (certify-only primary, signing subkey) is in the test vectors. Card curves Ghostly accepts: Ed25519, NIST P-256/384/521, brainpool, RSA ≥ 2048; secp256k1 is refused. Not tested on a physical card. **PIV / SSH: candidate signer profiles**, with different policies and formats from FIDO.

title: Ledger
body:
**Confirmed official capability/source**

[Bitcoin Signer Kit](https://developers.ledger.com/docs/device-interaction/dmk-ts/references/signers/btc) documents messages, PSBT and transactions

**Runtime / physical route**

Device Management Kit and installed Bitcoin app; USB/Bluetooth route must be checked per device/platform

**Restriction and Ghostly gate**

**New suggestion / candidate**. Pin app/device policy support and descriptor/PSBT versions, confirm outputs and fees; message support does not automatically imply Ghostly/Nostr/BIP322 compatibility.

title: COLDCARD
body:
**Confirmed official capability/source**

[PSBT signing](https://coldcard.com/docs/ready-to-sign/), [BIP322 support](https://coldcard.com/docs/bip322/)

**Runtime / physical route**

USB/file/MicroSD/NFC or Q QR, model-dependent

**Restriction and Ghostly gate**

**New suggestion / candidate**. Current BIP322 docs distinguish completed vs older draft flow and firmware requirements. Validate exact format, message limits, QR reassembly and device review; no funds/signatures requested now.

title: Blockstream Jade
body:
**Confirmed official capability/source**

[official firmware/source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Blockstream/Jade/master/README.md), [device documentation](https://help.blockstream.com/blockstream-jade)

**Runtime / physical route**

Candidate native/hardware or QR integration; select exact device transport/API

**Restriction and Ghostly gate**

**New suggestion / research** for Bitcoin/Liquid. Need supported signing/message matrix, firmware pin, blinding-data and authorization review. Do not assume parity with Trezor or generic PSBT transport.

title: Text, presence and typing
body:
**Composition and provider/runtime options**

Current 400 chat; transient presence/typing should be separately advertised with TTL and privacy preferences

**Dependencies and criteria for readiness**

Authenticated session, per-sender sequence/limits, reconnect semantics and no durable typing log by default. “Online” is a hint, not proof a person is available.

title: Files and attachments
body:
**Composition and provider/runtime options**

Current 500 / chat files/2 ([501](501-paired-files.md)); future disk streaming, range resume and storage adapters

**Dependencies and criteria for readiness**

Integrity digest, byte limits, receiver consent and durable receipt; current retry restarts the file, not a range resume. File delivery need not imply permanent backup.

title: Voice/video/screenshare
body:
**Composition and provider/runtime options**

Existing 600 legacy media; WebRTC capture/codec profile; native and mobile variants to validate

**Dependencies and criteria for readiness**

Permissions, device lifecycle, media encryption and capability negotiation; test each profile/runtime. Group mesh/SFU and recording are separate decisions, including who can decrypt.

title: Private groups
body:
**Composition and provider/runtime options**

**Current:** 900 with the [group mesh profile](9xx-group-mesh.md): one admin per epoch, signed commit chain, epoch secrets sealed per member, welcome/remove/role/rotate, a mesh of roster-derived pairwise edges, text only

**Dependencies and criteria for readiness**

Shipped for up to eight members with unit and four-browser tests (removal, offline catch-up from authors' logs, admin transfer, forks). Next: multiple admins, member key updates, files/media/payments behind their own group capabilities, native transports on edges, a store for members never online together. The eight-member cap is a first-profile bound, not measured capacity. A second profile, [group community](9xx-group-community.md), takes a group whose link is the way in to 256 members, with admission by any member and elected hubs; its cap is what a headless load test measured.

title: Group crypto
body:
**Composition and provider/runtime options**

**Decided for the first profile:** epoch secrets sealed with X25519 per member, HKDF keys, XChaCha20-Poly1305 with signed envelopes, confirmation tags; [MLS RFC9420](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9420.html) evaluated and not adopted at this size

**Dependencies and criteria for readiness**

Forward secrecy per epoch and post-compromise security on removal/rotation are tested; a compromised member seed is healed by removal, not rotation. Revisit MLS if groups grow past the mesh, or when member key updates are needed.

title: Channels / topics / forums
body:
**Composition and provider/runtime options**

Group or public content schemas, threading, replies, moderation and history policy

**Dependencies and criteria for readiness**

Not every topic is a separate transport/group key. Define audience, post authority, deletion/moderation semantics, indexing and spam quotas.

title: Password / payment-gated access
body:
**Composition and provider/runtime options**

Admission policy above 800/900 and 200; user-defined roles and expiring entitlements

**Dependencies and criteria for readiness**

Password is not a shared permanent group key; resist guessing with appropriate reviewed protocol/rate policy. Payment confirmation can authorize admission but does not cryptographically erase past content after expiry/removal. Refund/dispute policy explicit.

title: Local state
body:
**Composition and provider/runtime options**

Current IndexedDB/history; future native database/filesystem abstraction

**Dependencies and criteria for readiness**

Transactional persistence, quotas, encryption-at-rest policy and schema migrations. [IndexedDB standard](https://www.w3.org/TR/IndexedDB/) is a storage API, not a backup guarantee.

title: Remote encrypted storage
body:
**Composition and provider/runtime options**

User's own service, scoped Pubky homeserver, object storage or consented peer provider

**Dependencies and criteria for readiness**

**Candidate family**: encrypt before upload, define keys/retention/size/integrity, provider deletion limits, quotas and independent restore. Pick exact API before claiming cross-provider compatibility.

title: Distributed storage
body:
**Composition and provider/runtime options**

Hypercore/Autobase research; **new suggestion** IPFS/content addressing

**Dependencies and criteria for readiness**

[IPFS persistence](https://docs.ipfs.tech/concepts/persistence/) requires retention/pinning; [privacy](https://docs.ipfs.tech/concepts/privacy-and-encryption/) needs separate encryption. Signed logs/content hashes do not mean confidentiality, availability or guaranteed erasure.

title: Backup / export / import / migration
body:
**Composition and provider/runtime options**

Versioned encrypted archive + optional remote replication, selective per-layer export

**Dependencies and criteria for readiness**

First-class requirement, beginning with payment recovery. Define included secrets/history/files/provider state, authenticated format, KDF, rollback detection, restore drill, incompatible versions and stolen-device revocation. Migrate without merging unrelated identities or replaying spent tokens.

title: Store-forward / offline sync
body:
**Composition and provider/runtime options**

Peer or service mailboxes, retained protected envelopes, reconciliation over any approved transport

**Dependencies and criteria for readiness**

Consent, quotas, expiry, dedup, sender/recipient receipts and anti-abuse; policies per conversation. Preserve DHT-only's bounded behavior rather than silently adding a server store.

title: Local HTTP / Bitcoin / Lightning services
body:
**Composition and provider/runtime options**

Existing 700 HTTP subset; future explicit service schemas for node query or payment request

**Dependencies and criteria for readiness**

Name-based allowlist, request/response bounds, local permission and client capabilities. Read-only chain query and wallet administration are separate authorities. Never expose broad node RPC or credentials through generic proxy by default.

title: SDK and manifests
body:
**Proposed deliverable**

Stable adapter interface, exact capability versions, runtime requirements, permissions, resources, licenses, publisher identity and dependency constraints

**Dependencies / trust boundary**

Separate discovery metadata from executable code. Versioned host ABI and conformance vectors; no undocumented private engine access.

title: Plugin sandbox
body:
**Proposed deliverable**

Restrict filesystem/network/UI/CPU/memory; broker sensitive APIs

**Dependencies / trust boundary**

**Research**: browser sandboxed origins/workers and **new suggestion** [WASI](https://wasi.dev/) components where suitable. A worker or WASM module alone is not a complete security boundary. Native plugins need process isolation/OS permissions.

title: Package authenticity and updates
body:
**Proposed deliverable**

Signed package hashes/manifests, publisher key rotation, lockfiles, review provenance, rollback protection and uninstall/export behavior

**Dependencies / trust boundary**

**New suggestion**: evaluate [TUF](https://theupdateframework.io/docs/overview/) for update metadata. A valid signature identifies a publisher; it does not certify a safe app. Permissions must be re-reviewed when expanded.

title: Mini-apps and games
body:
**Proposed deliverable**

Chess, a racing game, shared tools and payment-request UI

**Dependencies / trust boundary**

App-specific shared state and authority; realtime routing may use transport 100. **New suggestion:** [Automerge](https://automerge.org/docs/hello/) for suitable collaborative state, not authoritative payment settlement or automatic anti-cheat. Chess turn order and racing latency need different models.

title: Marketplaces / hosting example
body:
**Proposed deliverable**

Discovery, offers, negotiated service terms and approved payments for hosting

**Dependencies / trust boundary**

Product composition, not a mandatory new WISP. Define delivery evidence, duration, availability, dispute/refund and moderation before paid deployment.

title: Multiple indexers
body:
**Proposed deliverable**

Query several independently chosen providers, provenance, freshness and disagreement display

**Dependencies / trust boundary**

Indexers rank/omit data differently. Preserve source assertions separately, avoid collapsing them into one “true” reputation score, and allow self-hosted/local sources.

title: Catalogs / curator stores
body:
**Proposed deliverable**

Family/capability search, publisher pages, runtime compatibility, reviews and warnings

**Dependencies / trust boundary**

Independent stores can curate differently. Installation permissions and package verification remain local; a catalog listing is not proof of conformance.

title: Reputation / trust
body:
**Proposed deliverable**

User-controlled source selection, signed reviews where appropriate, context-specific reputation

**Dependencies / trust boundary**

Identity linkage and Sybil resistance require explicit policy; do not infer personal trust from a payment or social follower count. Show conflicts and evidence origin.

title: Paid plugins / indexers
body:
**Proposed deliverable**

Optional licensing/access/subscriptions and payments through 200

**Dependencies / trust boundary**

Non-paying core remains composable as a design objective; expiry, offline license verification, refunds, cancellation and key loss require review. Paid ranking must be identified as such.

title: GhostlyOS
body:
**Proposed deliverable**

Long-term headless/runtime composition of adapters, apps, policies, local data and UI clients

**Dependencies / trust boundary**

Start with a service runtime rather than assume a new kernel/distribution. Process supervision, encrypted persistence, remote admin, upgrades, logs and backups need their own threat model.

title: Self-hosted 24h
body:
**Proposed deliverable**

Raspberry Pi/ARM64, x86 host, Docker and Umbrel packaging candidates

**Dependencies / trust boundary**

[Umbrel packaging](https://github.com/getumbrel/umbrel-apps) is an upstream route, not an installed Ghostly app. Test boot/crash recovery, disk full, resource limits, key custody and remote access; relay/listener exposure is explicit.

title: Future clients
body:
**Proposed deliverable**

React Native, improved PWA behavior, CLI/daemon tooling and plugin hosts

**Dependencies / trust boundary**

Each advertises what it actually supports. Native SDK availability is not proof of a Ghostly mobile integration, background delivery, battery performance or App Store acceptance.
